How, and why: Maximum Willpower reduced permanently, by the sum of the Willpower costs of every inscribed spell. Not spent. Reduced.

Section: Why the site cannot do this today
How, and why: Willpower maximum is derived: 2 a point of Mind, plus whatever items and cards add. Every input is an addition. There is no subtraction anywhere in deriveStats, and no concept of a permanent character debt.
It is still a derived number. Sum the Willpower cost of the inscribed list and subtract. One more term in the same expression, with a negative sign. The hard part is not the maths.

The inscribed list is durable character state that changes the sheet outside of a fight, and removing a rune has to give the maximum back exactly. So the list is the record and the number is always computed from it, never stored. Store the number and one bad edit costs a player their Willpower for good.
A Runebearer block listing each rune: the spell, its cost, whether it has fired since the last Long Rest. The block header carries the total borrowed, so a player can see what the scars cost.

A Short Rest brings back runes whose costs add to no more than Physique. That is a budget spend against a list, which is the same interaction the Cauldron Keeper already has when choosing essences into a brew.

RUNIC NETWORK and STREAMLINED PATTERNS add Physique back to the maximum. So a late Runebearer is Mind-derived Willpower, minus the runes, plus a Physique. All three terms in one expression, and the order does not matter because they are all additive.

A player who inscribes to the point of zero maximum Willpower. Nothing stops them, and at zero they cannot cast anything that is not a rune. That might be a legitimate build. Worth a floor, or worth a warning, but it should not be a silent trap.

Section: What this shares with the others
How, and why: The Arcanist wants a list with a computed cap. The Spellquill wants a shelf of prepared things. This wants a list that feeds a derived number. Three different shelves, and only this one reaches into the stat block.
